picks.why: JPM trades at 15.7x trailing earnings with EPS up 13.4%, has among the lowest weekly volatility on the list (2.12%), has already reported, and is the cleanest way to own what the synthesis calls the only sector that a 4.52% 10Y and a steeper curve help.
At 11.0x trailing with EPS still up 10.1%, this best-in-class auto underwriter is one of the cheapest sound businesses on the table, has already reported, and earns more on its float as yields rise.

EPS rose 6.2% while the price fell 10.9% over twelve weeks, leaving this 52-year dividend grower at 16.4x trailing with a 4.27% yield per the synthesis, already reported and low in volatility, so the multiple fell and the business did not.

UNH has already reported a beat and, per the synthesis, raised its FY26 guide twice, yet it trades at 22.9x trailing on trough earnings (trailing EPS still 26.1% below the prior four quarters) with 2.74% weekly volatility, a middling multiple on earnings that are recovering.

The synthesis names SPG the cheapest REIT at 15.4x with a 3.98% yield (the table's 43.8x is a GAAP multiple that depreciation inflates for any REIT), and it is a strong-balance-sheet owner of domestic property cash flow that does not report until Aug 10.

summary: This is a low-volatility book of cheap, sound businesses with no binary events this week, because each has already reported or reports weeks from now: two financials that the higher 10Y helps (JPM, PGR), a staple whose price fell while its earnings rose (PEP), a managed-care recovery with a twice-raised guide (UNH), and the synthesis's cheapest REIT (SPG). I skipped every name reporting this week, the energy war premium and the AI-reset trade, and NVDA stays on watch until the FOMC and mega-cap guidance clear the gate the synthesis describes. I have no memory of how this week went and used none.
